title: Mini vs Full Tummy Tuck: Which One Do You Need?
meta_description: A mini treats loose skin below the belly button; a full treats the whole abdomen and usually repairs muscles. How to tell which you need.
excerpt: A mini treats loose skin below the belly button, while a full treats the whole abdomen and in most cases repairs separated muscles. Here is how they compare on scar, belly button, muscle repair and recovery, and the questions that help you and your surgeon choose.
quick_answer:
What is the difference between a mini and a full tummy tuck?

A mini treats loose skin below the belly button and leaves a scar of about 3 to 6 inches (Cleveland Clinic). A full runs from hip bone to hip bone, may add a scar around the belly button and, in most cases, repairs separated muscles (ASPS). Where your loose skin sits helps decide.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck Scar, last updated 08/16/2022
quotes: The scar for a standard tummy tuck usually spans your abdomen, from hip bone to hip bone, just above your pubic area. You may also have a scar around your belly button.

A mini tummy tuck is for people who have a small amount of excess fat and tissue beneath their belly button. The scar is shorter than a full tummy tuck scar. It's about the length of a C-section scar (between 3 inches and 6 inches).

sources.title: Tummy Tuck (Abdominoplasty), last updated 01/30/2024
quotes: In a mini tummy tuck, there's generally no cut around the belly button.
A shorter procedure, like a mini abdominoplasty, usually results in a smaller scar.

sources.publisher: ASPS website, a post by Samir Rao, MD
sources.title: Understanding the different types of tummy tucks
quotes: A traditional tummy tuck is the most common type of abdominoplasty, focusing on both the upper and lower abdomen.
Standard tummy tucks are best for men and women who want to firm and tighten the area above and below the belly button. It can also help people who have separated abdominal muscles
Most patients can return to nonstrenuous work after a couple of weeks, but it takes around three months to fully recover from a tummy tuck.
It improves only the area below the belly button, removing lax skin and strengthening muscles in the lower stomach.
Most people can return to work one to two weeks after surgery and resume more vigorous activities in about five to six weeks. The trade-off is that its results are limited to the lower abdomen.
An extended tummy tuck is best if you have a lot of excess and sagging skin on your abdomen and flanks. It uses a longer incision that stretches up and around the flanks
You'll typically need about four to six weeks of downtime before returning to work and about 12 weeks more to return to strenuous activities.
